strengths: The authors propose a novel way to learn options directly from neural networks that are learning or have been retrained.
The overall presentation is rigorous as well as the empirical evaluation (10 seeds with 95% CI).
The method seems to perform better compared to proposed baselines.
The originality of the method in discovering options, with potential to learn options from legacy agents and integrate unusual ways of learning options/skills.
Inferring skills/options provides an intuitive and principled way of extracting options from pretrained neural network policies based on activation regions.
The idea of directly extracting options from NN policies instead of constructing them during training appears novel and interesting, possibly first paper, and may lead to further research.
Experimental results look very promising with the proposed approach outperforming existing baselines for constructing options as well as transfer learning approaches.
The paper is well-written and examples are provided to illustrate key concepts.
The approach is original in extracting options from an already trained neural network.
weaknesses: The presentation is heavy and sometimes confusing.
The HRL baseline of Option-Critic is outdated and does not reflect progress in the field.
The qualitative experiments are very limited.
Sections 4.1 and 4.2 require major rewriting; many references to oblique trees are obscure; visualization (Figure 1) is insufficient; notation of Z is confusing and may be unnecessary.
Scalability: the total number of options is exponential in network size, leading to combinatorial explosion and computational expense; exhaustive search is a bottleneck.
Experiments are limited to grid world environments, lacking complex or continuous domains, limiting evidence of generalizability.
The number of sub-policies raises exponentially with neural network size, limiting the approach to very small networks; scalability is not adequately addressed.
It is unclear whether the subset selection step is better than selecting from random policies; missing ablation comparison with a random baseline.
